title: Johnson cardinality bound for admissible constant-weight codes
statement: Let $n \ge 1$, $d \ge 1$, and suppose $2d \le n$. If $C$ is an $(n,d,w)$-admissible code — a finite set of binary words of length $n$ in which any two distinct words are at Hamming distance at least $d$ and every word has weight at most $w$ — and the weight bound satisfies $w \le J_2(n,d)$, where $J_2(n,d) = \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(n - \sqrt{n(n-2d)}\bigr)$, then $\abs{C} \le 2n$.
hypotheses_covered: C is an (n,d,w)-admissible code (min distance ≥ d, weights ≤ w)
replaced:
Assume $n > 0$, $1 \le d$ and $2d \le n$. Every $(n,d,w)$-admissible code $C$ with
$w \le J_2(n,d)$ satisfies $\abs{C} \le 2n$.
